title: Metric contracts and lifecycle for inference pipelines
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical working doc to define metric contracts, tracing span expectations, and dashboard sketches for inference pipelines (router -> tokenizer -> model-server -> kv-cache -> emitter). Goal is to make sure engineers deploying or changing serving code can rely on stable metric names/labels and know how to add observability for rollout/change management.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private runtime components (routing, model servers, L7 edge, prefix cache).
- Focuses on signals used for SLOs, cost attribution, and regression detection: request counts, latencies, token counts, cache hit/miss, model load/eviction, GPU utilization (high-level), and error breakdowns.

Who should care:
- Serving/runtime engineers adding instrumentation
- SRE/oncall and incident responders
- Product owners for rollout/quality tracking
- Cost engineering for efficiency dashboards

High-level principles (contract rules):
1) Names follow namespace: ri.inference.<component>.<signal> (ri = redwood inference). Examples: ri.inference.router.requests_total, ri.inference.modelserver.tokens_emitted_total
2) Labels: model (model_short_name), model_revision, deployment (deployment_id), region, tier (hosted/dedicated/private), gpu_type (if applicable), route (api route or service route), rollout_id, quantization_profile. Keep label cardinality low; prefer stable enumerations.
3) Units: all metrics MUST have explicit units in the help/description: seconds, tokens, bytes, percent. Histograms use seconds (or bytes). Counts are pure integers.
4) Backwards-compatibility: Never remove a metric name; deprecate via suffix _deprecated and introduce new names, keep both exported for 90 days.
5) Metric ownership: each metric must declare an owner (email) in code comments / registration file.

Core metric definitions (recommended set):
- ri.inference.router.requests_total  (counter)
  labels: {route, result: {ok,error,rate_limited,quota_exceeded,fallback}}
  description: total API requests received by router.

- ri.inference.router.request_duration_seconds (histogram)
  labels: {route, result, model}
  buckets: [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1.0,2.5,5.0]
  SLI mapping: p95 <= 250ms for short-form routes; adjust per-route SLA.

- ri.inference.tokens_emitted_total (counter)
  labels: {model, deployment, request_type}
  description: number of generation tokens emitted (post-processed). Important for billing and cost SLOs.

- ri.inference.kv_cache_hits_total / ri.inference.kv_cache_misses_total (counters)
  labels: {model, cache_key_type, deployment}
  note: expose current cache_size_bytes (gauge) and cache_entries_total (gauge).

- ri.inference.model_load_latency_seconds (histogram)
  labels: {model, model_revision, gpu_type, deployment}
  description: time to load model into process/GPU. Alert if > expected baseline (depends on model size).

- ri.inference.request_tokens_in (histogram/counter)
  labels: {route, model, deployment}
  description: tokens in request (for request-size SLIs and billing).

- ri.inference.errors_total (counter)
  labels: {component, code, cause}
  description: unit errors per component (tokenizer, modelserver, router). Use canonical codes (HTTP 5xx/4xx and internal codes).

- ri.inference.oom_evictions_total (counter)
  labels: {model, gpu_type, node_id}
  description: GPU memory OOM evictions; critical for capacity planning.

- ri.inference.gpu_utilization_percent (gauge)
  labels: {node_id, gpu_type, deployment}
  description: aggregated % utilization for cost dashboards.

Histogram and bucket guidance:
- Prefer a shared set of latency buckets for downstream aggregation. Keep buckets small in critical low-latency ranges (ms) for frontend-facing routes.
- Use explicit quantiles sparingly at export-time; prefer histograms + Prometheus recording rules to compute pXX.

Label cardinality rules (practical):
- model_revision can be high-cardinality; only include when necessary for rollout investigations. If included, add a fallback label like model_revision_bucketed = {stable, canary, unknown}.
- node_id or instance_id should not be used in long-term metrics; used for ephemeral debugging panels only via a separate debug export prefix (ri.debug.*).

Tracing: span taxonomy and sampling
- Span naming: ri.span.<component>.<operation> (example: ri.span.modelserver.infer, ri.span.router.route-match)
- Required span attributes (trace-level): trace_id, request_id, rollout_id, model, model_revision (optional), route, region, deployment, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_microcents (approx).
- Parent-child model: client -> edge -> router -> tokenizer -> modelserver (load + infer) -> emitter. Ensure trace context not dropped at async boundaries (e.g., Kafka or worker queues) — preserve trace parent in message metadata.
- Sampling policy: default 0.2% sampling for production traffic, automatic 100% sampling for: errors (span.status != OK), requests with latency > 2s, requests with outlier token counts (> 95th percentile), and requests tagged with rollout_id != stable. For heavy debug windows we can enable higher sampling via a remote-config flag.
- Tagging and privacy: do not include PII in spans. If prompts are recorded for debug, store redacted versions in a separate secure blob and link via non-guessable debug_blob_id in the trace.

Dashboard sketches (panels and drilldowns)
- Overview dashboard (service: inference-overview):
  - Global request rate (rps) over time (by route and tier).
  - p50/p95/p99 latency lines per route (PromQL examples left as notes).
  - token throughput (tokens/s) and tokens per request histogram.
  - error breakdown pie (5xx/4xx/validation/error-codes).
  - GPU utilization heatmap (by region).

- Cost & efficiency dashboard (tokens-to-gpu):
  - tokens emitted per GPU-second (by model and region).
  - median tokens per request vs model size (to detect expensive small responses).
  - cache hit ratio and estimated cost savings (simple model: saved_tokens * token_cost).

- Rollout impact dashboard (per-rollout):
  - compare p95 latency, error rate, token-efficiency between rollout cohorts (rollout_id label).
  - auto-calculated regression flags if metric delta > X% and statistically significant.

- Debugging panels (debug only, not on alerting dashboards):
  - traces sampled per minute, trace latency histogram, top slowest spans (grouped by component).
  - OOM events timeline and correlated host metrics.

Alerting guidance (examples):
- page if p95 latency for any route > 2x baseline and requests_total > 10 rps for 5m.
- page on error rate > 1% sustained for 5m for high-volume routes.
- page on OOM evictions > 1 in 10m.
- ticket (non-page) for sustained drop in cache-hit ratio > 15% vs baseline.

Instrumentation checklist for engineers (copy into PRs):
- [ ] Add metric with ri.inference.<component>.* name and unit in help string.
- [ ] Add owner comment and GitHub issue/PR reference in registration.
- [ ] Use low-cardinality labels only; document any new label and justify.
- [ ] Add histogram buckets matching shared bucket set.
- [ ] Emit trace/span with required attributes and ensure trace context propagation.
- [ ] Add unit/integration test that validates metrics emit (can use test harness in runtime repo).
- [ ] Add dashboard panel suggestion in PR description (optional for small changes).

Migration / rollout pattern for metric changes:
- Add new metric name in code alongside old one for at least 90 days.
- Create recording rules to copy/aggregate new metric into the old name for downstream panels during migration window.
- When deprecating a label, leave a noop label emission path for a period and mark label as deprecated in registration.

Examples / PromQL snippets (notes to self)
- p95 latency for route api.v1.chat:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ri_inference_router_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"api.v1.chat\"}[5m])) by (le))
- cache hit ratio: rate(ri_inference_kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / (rate(ri_inference_kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(ri_inference_kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))
- tokens per GPU-second (approx): sum(rate(ri_inference_tokens_emitted_total[5m])) by (gpu_type) / sum(rate(node_gpu_seconds_total[5m])) by (gpu_type)

Operational notes / gotchas:
- watch out for prometheus label explosion from model_revision; prefer stable model_short_name in dashboards and have a separate "per-revision" debug dashboard.
- async workers must preserve trace parent ID in queue/topic metadata. Several past incidents were traced to lost context.
- Recording rules should live alongside service prometheus config in infra repo to ensure reproducible queries for grafana.

Open questions (action items):
- Decide canonical list of rollout_id semantics: should it be a stable label across requests within a rollout? (Action: convo with release-engineering)
- Agree on exact default sampling rate per environment (prod 0.2% suggested) and a simple feature flag to bump sampling for a tenant. (Action: SRE + runtime)
- Formalize cost-estimate labeling (we emit cost_estimate_microcents in traces now as experimental) — who owns unit assumptions? (Action: finance + runtime)

Related links / references:
- CON-4321 (metrics naming RFC)
- JIRA-OBS-78 (trace sampling improvements)
- runtime PR #912 (initial metric registration utils)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Push shared histogram buckets into runtime metrics helper and document in README.
- Add quickstart snippet for adding a metric + trace in the runtime repo (example endpoint).
- Run a 2-week experiment with higher trace sampling for the canary environment and evaluate signal quality.

-- end --
